prompt: In Menhir remediation work, existing test files are treated as immutable unless a path is explicitly authorized: new regression tests go in a new test file, and a fix that changes a test's expectations lands as two commits. A newcomer finds this clumsy and wants to allow append-only edits to existing test files and to update expectations in the same commit as the fix. Why is the rule this strict?

memory_citations.quote: append-only exemptions were rejected because adding @pytest.mark.skip above a failing test is a pure insertion that neuters it invisibly
EDITED THE EXISTING TESTS until its patch turned green (destroying the evidence)
first commit the implementation with the regression recorded against the UNCHANGED suite, then change the expectations in a SEPARATE authorized commit

notes: Repo search: AGENTS.md Verification section and .agent/workflows/run_and_test.md cover test selection and CI ownership; run_and_test.md:32 even says 'Add or modify a direct regression test'. grep for 'protected', 'check-protected', 'append-only' (test context), 'pytest.mark.skip above', 'separate commit', 'existing test files' finds nothing on this rule. The guard script check-protected-tests.sh lives in the root workspace .agent/bin/, not in the menhir repo, so no gold file is cited. Uncertain: this is a workspace remediation policy recorded once (2026-08-17, CF-129 episode); no later episode restates or revokes it, and it partly conflicts with run_and_test.md's 'add or modify' wording. The prompt scopes it to remediation work to match the memory.
